provenance.title: HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis — eligibility, the acute-infection exclusion, and follow-up retesting
provenance.primarySource: WHO Consolidated guidelines on HIV prevention (PrEP), carried into the 2021 consolidated HIV guidelines
provenance.why: PrEP prevents HIV in a person who is HIV-negative and at substantial ongoing risk. Two things make it unsafe if skipped: starting PrEP in someone with undiagnosed acute HIV exposes a single-class regimen to replicating virus and breeds resistance, so acute infection must be excluded first; and a person on PrEP must be retested regularly, because seroconversion on PrEP that is not caught continues a resistance-selecting regimen. So PrEP is prophylaxis wrapped in two safety checks, not a prescription.

sourceVerification.note: The WHO HIV DAK is NOT vendored under docs/reference/who-dak/MANIFEST.json. Authored against the published PrEP guidance; ships ENGINEERING_SEED until the primary text is vendored. The definition of 'substantial risk' and the exact retest interval are national-guideline decisions; the structure here (negative status required, exclude acute infection, retest on a schedule) is WHO-invariant.

rules.name: HIV-positive — PrEP is not indicated, this is treatment
rules.message: PrEP is not indicated — the person is HIV-positive and needs treatment, not prophylaxis.
rules.explanation: PrEP is a two-drug prophylaxis for HIV-negative people. Given to an HIV-positive person it is functional monotherapy against replicating virus and selects resistance. An HIV-positive result means HIV care and ART, not PrEP.
rules.requiredAction: Do not start or continue PrEP. Enrol in HIV care and start ART.
sourceRefs: WHO PrEP guidance — PrEP is for HIV-negative people only

adaptation.whoStatement: PrEP is contraindicated in HIV-positive individuals, who require ART.

testCases.name: unknown status never reads as safe-to-PrEP here

rules.name: Symptoms of acute HIV — exclude acute infection before starting PrEP
rules.message: Exclude acute HIV before starting PrEP — recent exposure with acute symptoms.
rules.explanation: A negative antibody test does not exclude very recent (acute) HIV, when the person is antibody-negative but viraemic. Starting PrEP then exposes a two-drug regimen to replicating virus. Recent high-risk exposure with acute symptoms warrants excluding acute infection (e.g. viral load / repeat testing) before PrEP.
rules.requiredAction: Delay PrEP initiation, exclude acute HIV (viral load or repeat testing per the window period), then start PrEP if still negative.
sourceRefs: WHO PrEP guidance — exclude acute HIV before initiation

adaptation.whoStatement: Acute HIV should be excluded before PrEP where recent exposure and symptoms are present.

testCases.name: negative but acute symptoms — exclude first
positive is handled by the other gate, not this one

rules.name: HIV-negative at substantial ongoing risk — offer PrEP
rules.message: Eligible for PrEP — HIV-negative, no acute infection, substantial ongoing risk.
rules.explanation: PrEP is offered to HIV-negative people at substantial ongoing risk of HIV once acute infection is excluded. Substantial risk is defined nationally; this rule fires only when the caller asserts it.
rules.requiredAction: Offer PrEP, enrol in an HIV_PREVENTION programme to record the course, and schedule the first follow-up HIV test.
sourceRefs: WHO PrEP guidance — offer to those at substantial risk

adaptation.whoStatement: PrEP should be offered to HIV-negative people at substantial risk of HIV infection.

testCases.name: negative, no acute, substantial risk is eligible
negative, no acute, low risk is not offered
acute symptoms — eligibility does not apply until excluded

rules.name: On PrEP — HIV retest due
rules.message: HIV retest due — a person on PrEP should be retested at least every 3 months.
rules.explanation: Seroconversion on PrEP that goes undetected continues a two-drug regimen against replicating virus and selects resistance. Regular retesting (at least 3-monthly) catches it and switches the person to full treatment.
rules.requiredAction: Perform an HIV test now. If positive, stop PrEP and start ART; if negative, continue PrEP and schedule the next test.
sourceRefs: WHO PrEP guidance — quarterly HIV testing on PrEP

adaptation.whoStatement: People on PrEP should be retested for HIV at least every 3 months.

testCases.name: not on PrEP — rule does not apply
